 Ilhan Omar slams ‘ungodly corruption’ behind targeted raid 
 by Alix Breeden 
 Staff 
 Thursday, October 22, 2026 at 4:00 PM PDT

 U.S. Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., speaks during a campaign event for Minnesota Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan, a Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate, at Cedar Field Park in Minneapolis on  Aug. 8. AP 
 Ten days after the Trump-led Department of Justice raided Rep. Ilhan Omar’s home , the Minnesota Democrat is speaking out. 
 In a sit-down interview with MS NOW , Omar recalled being woken up around 6 AM after getting to bed just three hours prior following a night of travel. But “pounding” at her front and back door, she told reporter Chris Hayes, was more of an intimidation tactic than anything else. 
 Community members rally in support of Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., on Oct. 12 at Powderhorn Park in Minneapolis. AP 
 “You don’t show up to somebody’s house that early in the morning unless you’re trying to freak them out. And you know it obviously did freak all of us out,” she told Hayes.
 The Justice Department, in a statement to MS NOW, called this a “judicially authorized search warrant” that was “part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation,” but Omar’s past statements against the sitting president may have made her a target as well.
 Donald Trump has repeatedly attacked the congresswoman, pushing vile conspiracies that she married her brother to gain U.S. citizenship. 
 “We ought to get her the hell out! She married her brother,” Trump claimed at a Pennsylvania rally in December 2025. “Therefore she’s here illegally.” 
 What followed was a crowd chanting, “Send her back.”
 Before the Oct. 12 raid, Omar received some foreshadowing of what was to come when she was notified that her immigration file was being looked into. 
 “I did hear that they opened, that there was an opening of my immigration file, but I didn’t know to the extent of what the opening of my investigation meant and who opened it,” she said.
 Related | Ilhan Omar stands strong in face of racist DHS raid 
 Omar arrived in the U.S. in 1995 at just 12 years old as her family sought to flee civil war in Somalia. She became a naturalized citizen in 2000 at age 17. 
 While her father was the main helper in filling out her paperwork, Omar called out the absurd conspiracy that somehow a 12-year-old had intentionally gamed the U.S. immigration system. 
 “It would be a huge undertaking to, I suppose, indict a 12-year-old for being so cleverly conspiring to defraud immigration services to come to the United States,” she told Hayes. “I’m sure there are a lot of smart 12-year-olds, but that seems like a leap.”
 Sources told MS NOW that the department was investigating whether Omar’s family made false claims about her age or other fraudulent claims when entering the U.S. 
 Jack Ohman/Tribune Content Agency 
 But the attack on Omar is just a piece of the overarching trend in which the president’s political foes find themselves in the crosshairs of his administration.
 Former FBI Director James Comey, who earned his ire from Trump during the investigation into Russian election interference , was indicted by the administration in 2025 in what was called “ vindictive persecution .” His supposed crime: sharing a photo of seashells forming the phrase “86 47.”
 Similarly, in 2025, Democrat Adam Schiff was also targeted by the president’s loyal Department of Justice over claims that the California senator had committed mortgage fraud . 
 And while the list of Trump’s targeted political foes continues, Omar is the first one to be targeted for deportation. 
 This, however, won’t stop her from fighting. 
 “In my faith teachings, we believe that God doesn’t give you more than you can handle,” she told the outlet. “If I continue to stand up to bullies and people who are carrying out ungodly corruption, I’m going to be okay.”
